newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends lower on profit-taking.

text.p: * Index ends a notch above the strong 3,300 support
Manila shares finished a tad down on Friday on widespread selling in thirdliner issues that posted gains during the week, traders said.
"Most of the punters who bought earlier in the week started selling most of their holdings," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
The main index dipped 8.45 points and closed at 3,301.98. It lost 20.32 points week-on-week from 3,322.30.
In the broad market, decliners beat gainers 86 to 53 with 66 issues unchanged. Volume was heavy at 35.54 billion shares valued at 3.685 billion pesos. All sub-indices closed down.
Although there was no action in firstliners for most of the session, San Miguel A saw some heavy buying in late trade which prevented the index from dropping below the 3,300 level.
San Miguel A ended 50 centavos up at 55.50 and was among the most actively traded issues of the day.
Thirdliners which posted losses with substantial volume were leisure firm Greater Asia Resources Corp, United Paragon Mining Co, and Itogon-Suyoc Mines.
The Dow's 93-point overnight drop depressed sentiment in the local bourse, said dealer Poch Zamora, at Peregrine Securities.
"Next week, there will still be plays on speculatives but there will be more concentration on blue chips which look ripe for the picking," said Diversified's Garcia.
